title: Accelerating Multi-GPU Embedding Retrieval with PGAS-Style Communication for Deep Learning Recommendation Systems
problem: Multi-GPU embedding retrieval in recommendation systems uses collective communication that incurs overhead from data unpacking and rearrangement, limiting communication-computation overlap and smooth network usage.
motivation: Efficient multi-GPU embedding retrieval is critical for scaling deep learning recommendation inference.
method: Instead of NCCL collective communication (the standard synchronized approach where all GPUs coordinate and reshape data), they use PGAS-style one-sided asynchronous messages where each GPU directly sends data to others without waiting. They build this into a custom CUDA embedding retrieval backend for PyTorch. This asynchronous approach eliminates synchronization overhead (the cost of GPUs waiting) and data restructuring costs (rearranging data).
key_novelty: Replace collective communication with PGAS-style one-sided asynchronous messaging (where each GPU directly sends data without waiting for coordination) for multi-GPU embedding retrieval.
contributions: PGAS-style GPU communication approach for multi-GPU embedding retrieval
CUDA/PyTorch backend implementation supporting PGAS communication scheme
1.97x weak-scaling and 2.63x strong-scaling speedup on 4-GPU NVLink systems
Better communication-computation overlap and smoother network utilization
limitations: Evaluation limited to 4-GPU NVLink systems; scalability to larger systems and other interconnects not discussed.
